title: The completion matrix validator: the ledger's own guards
note: This file is not a subsystem, it is the thing that decides whether the other rows are telling the truth -- so it is in the trust boundary for every completion claim this repository makes, and a guard here that quietly stopped working would be invisible in exactly the way that matters most. C1-C4 attack the boundary vocabulary, which is the cheapest available route to a finished matrix over an unfinished system: move a sentence from residual_gaps to boundaries and the row goes COMPLETE with nothing else changed. C5-C8 attack the checks that keep a row's evidence its own -- COMPLETE with gaps still listed, COMPLETE with no mutation coverage, borrowed coverage, a hosted claim with no run behind it. C9-C10 attack the two staleness guards, which exist because twelve rows were once found describing subsystems that had been built months earlier.

mutations.name: C1_a_boundary_may_describe_work
mutations.find:
for phrase in _WORK_PHRASES:
                if phrase in low:
mutations.rationale: 'not implemented' becomes a stateable limit, and every unfinished row can be closed by moving one sentence between two fields

mutations.name: C2_absent_testing_is_a_limit_under_any_reason
mutations.find: if hit and reason not in _TESTABILITY_REASONS:
mutations.rationale: 'architecturally intended' starts explaining why a test was never written, which it cannot do: it explains absent behaviour, not absent coverage of behaviour that is there

mutations.name: C3_every_reason_can_excuse_absent_testing
mutations.rationale: same loophole as C2 by the other route, and the more likely one: widening a set reads as tidying up

mutations.name: C4_a_boundary_needs_no_argument
mutations.find: if not isinstance(detail, str) or len(detail.strip()) < 80:
mutations.replace: if not isinstance(detail, str) or len(detail.strip()) < 0:
mutations.rationale: a boundary becomes an assertion with nothing behind it, which is how unfinished work gets reclassified as a limit of what is possible

mutations.name: C5_a_detail_may_restate_the_limit
mutations.find: elif detail.strip() in limit or limit.strip() in detail:
mutations.rationale: the evidence requirement is satisfied by copying the claim into the evidence field

mutations.name: C6_complete_may_keep_its_residual_gaps
mutations.rationale: the one arithmetic relation the whole matrix rests on -- COMPLETE means no gaps -- stops being enforced, and 39/39 can be declared over a list of open work

mutations.name: C7_complete_needs_no_mutation_coverage
mutations.rationale: a row can claim completion with tests that would pass if the enforcement they cover were deleted

mutations.name: C8_complete_needs_no_boundaries
mutations.find:
if not bounds:
                    # The classification says
mutations.rationale: the classification says 'complete to current technically defensible LIMIT' and the limit stops having to be stated, which is the easiest way to overstate a system

mutations.name: C9_a_hosted_claim_needs_no_run_id
mutations.rationale: 'green' and 'should be fine' become hosted evidence -- the one kind of claim a reader cannot check for themselves

mutations.name: C10_stale_prose_about_built_subsystems_is_accepted
mutations.find:
named = {m for m in modules
                         if len(m) > 4 and m in low}
mutations.rationale: restores the state twelve rows were found in: 'the scheduler does not exist yet', months after it did

mutations.name: C11_stale_coverage_claims_are_accepted
mutations.find: hits = {t for t in _fuzz_targets() if _fuzz_gap_names(low, t)}
mutations.rationale: a row stays out of COMPLETE for fuzzing that was already written, which understates the system while looking rigorous

mutations.name: C12_borrowed_mutation_coverage_is_accepted
mutations.rationale: a row cites a spec that mutates somebody else's code, and the coverage claim is about a file the row does not own
